title: Shifting the Reciprocal Hyperbola Up and Right
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = 1 / x is to be shifted up 1 unit and right 1 unit. Give an equation for the shifted graph and describe its asymptotes and intercepts.

steps.title: Apply the Horizontal Shift (Right 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Replace x with x - 1 in y = 1/x to shift the hyperbola 1 unit to the right.
steps.why: Horizontal translation right by 1 unit moves the vertical asymptote from x = 0 to x = 1.

steps.title: Apply the Vertical Shift (Up 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Add 1 to the right-hand side (or replace y with y - 1) to shift the hyperbola 1 unit upward.
steps.why: Vertical translation upward by 1 unit moves the horizontal asymptote from y = 0 to y = 1.

steps.title: Describe the Asymptotes and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The original hyperbola y = 1/x has asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0. The shifted hyperbola has vertical asymptote x = 1, horizontal asymptote y = 1, and passes through the origin (0, 0) and (2, 2).
steps.why: Both coordinate-axis asymptotes translate by the shift vector (1, 1).
